data.narrative:
Orbital Inc., a seed-stage Space & Aerospace company founded by Euwyn Poon, operates within a sector containing 5 public comparables (RKLB, PL, LUNR, ASTS, SATL) and 8 identifiable private peers including SpaceX and Rocket Lab. The company participated in Andreessen Horowitz's Speedrun program but has not publicly disclosed total capital raised.

Stage-progression analysis provides the only applicable valuation method. Using a $16 million proxy derived from total raised as the base and applying a 2.5x multiplier typical of seed-to-next-stage progression yields an implied valuation of $40 million. Peer-median triangulation cannot be applied due to insufficient same-stage or adjacent-stage comparables in the Space & Aerospace sector; while 14 same-sector peers exist overall, zero meet the three-datapoint minimum threshold when filtered for stage relevance. Public-comp anchoring likewise cannot be deployed, as Orbital's revenue remains undisclosed—a standard constraint for private companies.

The analysis supports a valuation range of $34–$46 million, centered on $40 million. This range reflects the stage-progression methodology alone and carries material uncertainty. The primary risk is that seed-stage multipliers in frontier aerospace may differ substantially from the 2.5x assumption, and the $16 million base itself lacks independent confirmation. The lack of observable private peer transactions at this stage further limits the precision of this estimate.
